claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of thin-film FeNiCrCoCu coatings is primarily controlled by formation of a continuous chromium-rich oxide film.
The chromium-rich oxide film forms in situ during elevated-temperature exposure.
The chromium-rich oxide film acts as a protective and lubricious barrier that reduces wear.
Pre-oxidation annealing at approximately 500°C under controlled oxygen partial pressure will promote formation of a continuous chromium-rich surface oxide.
Pre-oxidation will improve wear performance relative to an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The as-deposited coating has a homogeneous microstructure.
Oxidation and diffusion processes are active during wear testing at 400–600°C under moderate-to-high contact loads.
The pre-oxidation treatment produces a stable, continuous, and adherent chromium-rich oxide film.
Copper may cause minor compositional modification of the chromium-rich oxide film.
The pre-formed oxide film reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
The pre-formed oxide film limits plastic deformation during high-temperature wear.
The pre-formed oxide film provides a lubricious interface.
The oxide-mediated interface mitigates both adhesive and abrasive wear.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have significantly lower wear volume than as-deposited coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have significantly lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings.
An intact, continuous chromium-rich oxide layer will correlate with enhanced wear resistance.
The proposed mechanism is applicable specifically at 400–600°C and under moderate-to-high loads.
